data.narrative:
Mesh Optical Technologies is a Series A chip design company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor players (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-chip firms including Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Cerebras at similar or adjacent stages.

Two methods prove applicable. Stage-Progression anchors to the $50M raised and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-round step-ups, implying $100M. Peer-Median triangulation uses 3 same-sector comparables: Rebellions at $2.3B, d-Matrix at $2.0B, and Positron AI at $1.0B. The median across these three peers is $2.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales cannot be applied absent revenue disclosure, which is standard for private companies in this sector. The semiconductor public median trades at 20.4x sales, but this method requires target financials not on file.

The two applicable methods produce a valuation range of $85M to $2.3B, with a triangulated median of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around stage interpretation—whether Mesh should be valued as an early Series A closer to stage-progression guidance ($100M) or as a competitive entrant in an overheated frontier-chip market anchored to recent peer rounds ($1.0B–$2.3B). Key uncertainties include capital efficiency, technology differentiation within optical interconnect, and path to revenue.
